judge_assessment.explanation: Every composition the judge says it checked is correct on my own recomputation: (f o g)(2) = f(6) = 10; the table's last column is (2x-1)^2 giving 1, 9, 25 at x = 0, 2, 3; (x-3)^2+1 = x^2-6x+10 against (x^2+1)-3 = x^2-2 for the two orders; (x+5)^2-2(x+5) = x^2+8x+15; 1/((x+2)-2) = 1/x; 2(x^2)+1 = 2x^2+1 against (2x+1)^2 = 4x^2+4x+1; (2x-1)+3 = 12 -> x=5; and both inverse directions collapse to x. The judge is also right that item 10 is properly open and that the key accepts multiple valid (f, g) pairs. Two things the judge missed. First, problem 2's table has TWO columns to fill - the middle column f(x) and the last column g(f(x)) - and verify.json id 2 covers only the last column; the key prints the middle column's three values ('Step 2. Middle column: f(0) = -1, f(2) = 3, f(3) = 5') with nothing behind them. That is the same shape as the acknowledged curr-032 finding: more printed answer slots than verify entries. Second, problem 7 ends 'then say in one phrase what the two answers show about order'; verify.json id 7 holds the two equiv checks and no manual entry, and the key answers it in Step 4 with no manual marker - while item 10, the only declared manual item, is marked correctly. Also worth recording: final_response.md describes all three PDFs but, unlike the other nine cases I reviewed in this batch, never names a filename for any of them.

strengths_to_preserve: The value-free 'composition machine' diagram in the directions (x -> g -> g(x) -> f -> f(g(x))) carries no numbers at all, so it is a picture of the WIRING rather than of one example, and problem 2's table then instantiates that wiring one input at a time before the sheet goes symbolic. The key's teaching note closes the loop explicitly: 'Reading the finished table left to right is exactly that rule, one input at a time.'

Problems 3 and 4 use the SAME f and g in both orders and sit adjacent, and the key does not just say composition is non-commutative - it hands the reader a one-input disproof ('ask the student to check one input, say x = 1: 4 versus -1'), which is a check the student can run without the key.

Problem 6's key note is unusually careful: after simplifying 1/((x+2)-2) to 1/x it points out that x = 0 must still be excluded 'because g(0) = 2 is exactly the input f cannot take'. The domain of a composition surviving simplification is the exact thing this problem type usually loses.

Item 10's key gives a model split, a SECOND valid split (g(x)=x^2 with f(x)=1/(x+6)), and a full-credit rule that requires the student to compose back - so the open item is graded on the justification, not on matching one answer.

root_causes.description: A tabular problem is verified column-wise at the author's discretion: the one-check-per-id rule is satisfied by whichever column the author chose, so the other column's cells print in the key with no backing check.
evidence: worksheet.pdf p.2 problem 2: the table has columns x, f(x), g(f(x)); the student fills the last two.
verify.json id 2 = three evals of (2*x - 1)**2 at x = 0, 2, 3 - the g(f(x)) column only.
answer_key.pdf p.1 problem 2 Step 2 prints f(0) = -1, f(2) = 3, f(3) = 5 with no verify entry behind them.

root_causes.description: A short written conclusion appended to a computational item ('say in one phrase what the two answers show about order') does not trigger a manual entry, because the manual rule is applied per problem rather than per requested response.
evidence: worksheet.pdf p.4 problem 7 final sentence; verify.json id 7 has two equiv entries and no manual entry.
answer_key.pdf p.3 problem 7 Step 4 supplies the conclusion with no manual marker, whereas problem 10 is explicitly headed 'Open response - many correct answers, flagged for manual review'.

root_causes.description: final_response.md names the three documents only generically and gives no filenames or paths, so the reader cannot connect the prose to the built PDFs. Eight of the ten cases in this batch print the ws_/ak_/ss_ filenames; this one and curr-399 do not.
evidence: final_response.md opens 'Three PDFs are ready: the student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a two-page study guide.' and contains no .pdf filename anywhere.
gate_log.txt does print the three built paths, so the information existed at delivery time.

improvements.title: Verify every cell a table asks the student to fill, not just the final column
improvements.proposed_change: State in SKILL.md that a table or multi-blank problem needs one check per FILLED CELL (or a manual entry), and enforce it in tests/check_answer_key.py by failing a problem segment whose printed answers outnumber its non-manual verify entries. Here that means three more evals under id 2 - eval('2*x - 1') at x = 0, 2 and 3 -> -1, 3, 5 - which also gives the Quick Answers bank the middle column it currently omits.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a verify JSON whose id 2 declares three evals plus an ak_ segment printing six answer values for that id. check_answer_key.py must exit 1 naming the unbacked values; it exits 0 today.
improvements.expected_impact: Input/output tables, two-column fill-ins and multi-feature analyses stop shipping half-checked, and the bank stops omitting answers the student was asked to produce.
improvements.risk: Counting 'printed answers' inside a worked narrative is noisier than counting boxes; scope the count to \boxed/\ans slots and let authors mark narrative intermediates plainly so they are not miscounted.

improvements.title: Give problem 7's one-phrase conclusion its own manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Apply the manual rule per requested response: when a stem appends 'say in one phrase/sentence what this shows', add {"id": N, "type": "manual", "desc": ...} beside the computational entries, exactly as item 10 already does. Record the acceptance criterion in desc ('names that the two composed rules differ, so composition is not commutative').
improvements.regression_test: Advisory lint in scripts/verify.py: a stem matching /say (in one|what) .*(phrase|sentence)|explain|justify/ under an id with no manual entry exits 2 with a named warning. Assert it fires for curr-381 problem 7 and stays silent for problems 1-6.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual count reported to the user matches the number of things a human actually has to read; short conclusions stop being graded by nobody.
improvements.risk: Minor noise increase on sheets that ask students to narrate every step; keep it advisory.

improvements.title: Name the three built PDFs by filename in final_response.md
improvements.proposed_change: Make the delivery step in SKILL.md require that final_response.md list each of the three artifacts by its actual built filename (the ws_/ak_/ss_ paths that build.sh already prints in the gate summary), not just by description. Eight of the ten cases in this batch already do this; the rule should be mandatory rather than habitual.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/check_artifact_health.py (or the eval scorer's delivery check) to fail when final_response.md contains no ws_*.pdf, ak_*.pdf and ss_*.pdf token. Run against curr-381's final_response.md: fails before the fix, passes after the filenames are added.
improvements.expected_impact: The reader can match each described document to a file without re-reading the build log.
improvements.risk: Filenames drift if the build is re-run with a different stem; generate the list from the gate summary rather than typing it.

case_summary: Ten correct, well-paced composition problems that genuinely use models: a numberless composition-machine diagram, an input/output table that instantiates it, then the same two rules composed both ways to make non-commutativity visible rather than asserted, and a two-sided inverse check that insists both directions are required. All symbolic work re-derived and correct, and item 10's open decomposition is handled exactly right - declared manual, with two valid model splits and a full-credit rule that demands composing back. Two coverage gaps the judge did not test: problem 2's table asks for two columns and verify.json checks only one, so the key's printed middle column (-1, 3, 5) is unbacked; and problem 7's closing one-phrase conclusion is answered in the key with no manual entry behind it. Delivery is also weaker than its siblings - final_response.md never names a single PDF filename.
